title: C# Questions & Answers - Continue, Goto Statements
sourceFile: Continue & Goto Statements - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on Continue and Goto Statements in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: continue is legal only inside a loop. An if statement is not a loop, so this is CS0139 (no enclosing loop out of which to continue).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: goto even: is a syntax error. A jump is written goto even; with a semicolon. The colon belongs on the label (even:), not on the goto.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
When i is 1, j = 1 is skipped (continue) and j = 2 is printed as "1 2". When i is 2, j = 1 is printed as "2 1" and j = 2 is skipped. j > 2 then breaks the inner for.

Output:

2 1

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: After the first entry, goto l1 jumps to i-- and then prints hi again. i only decreases, so the outer while is never re-tested in a way that can stop, and the inner while always finds j == 0. The program prints hi forever.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
i == 0 is true, so control jumps to the label and prints HI... once. There is no loop back to the label.

Output:

HI...

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Each goto l1 restarts the outer while after i has been incremented. First pass: i becomes 1 and "loop" is printed. Second pass: i becomes 2 and "loop" is printed again. Then i < 2 is false, so the program stops.

Output:

loop

loop
